title: Tenant-boundary routing mode refactor for EU residency & tiered fallback variants
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: our current routing decision path conflates tenant-level residency requirements (EU-only) with global tier routing and model-variant fallbacks. This has produced edge cases where a tenant with an EU-only contract will be routed to a lower-cost cross-region fallback during capacity pressure, violating residency guarantees. Goal: refactor the tenant-boundary routing mode so residency constraints are enforced as an immutable routing constraint, while still allowing safe tiered fallbacks within the permitted scope (compatible model variants hosted in EU regions or private deployments). The work includes: (1) a decision graph change in the policy evaluator to surface residency as an early hard constraint; (2) a routing-mode flag per-tenant that encodes allowlists/denylists for region and tier combinations; (3) an expanded model-variant compatibility table that marks which fallbacks are residency-preserving; (4) runtime checks and instrumentation for emergency passthrough when no compliant capacity exists; (5) a migration plan for existing tenants and tests for regressions.
acceptance_criteria: Tenant metadata supports a new 'residency_mode' enum (EU_ONLY, PREFER_EU, GLOBAL) and a per-tenant allowlist/denylist for region tiers
Policy evaluator short-circuits with ResidencyFailure when request region would violate EU_ONLY tenants
Fallback selector only considers model variants and regions that preserve declared residency; cross-border fallbacks must be opt-in via an emergency override flag with audit logging
End-to-end tests covering capacity shortage scenarios: dedicated pool saturated, hosted EU pool saturated, and emergency override path
Migration script to backfill residency_mode for existing tenants and a compatibility shim for one release
